summary: Russia launched a massive overnight drone attack with 186 Shahed, Gerbera, and Parodyya UAVs from seven directions, including 72 jet-powered variants; Ukrainian air defenses destroyed or suppressed 161 drones, with hits recorded at 18 locations and debris at six. Jet-powered UAVs penetrated deep into Ukrainian airspace, tracked from Bryansk into Chernihiv, over Kyiv suburbs, across the Dnipro River, and throughout central and eastern oblasts. Explosions struck the Russian Baltic Fleet base in Baltiysk and a Russian cargo ship near Gelendzhik, while Ukraine and the UK agreed on joint long-range drone production.
key_points: Russia launched 186 strike UAVs overnight from Orel, Kursk, Millerovo, Shatalovo, Primorsko-Akhtarsk, occupied Donetsk, and occupied Crimea; 161 were destroyed or suppressed including 56 jet-powered Shaheds. (Source: @kpszsu/98362)
Jet-powered UAVs maneuvered across Chernihiv, Kyiv, Zhytomyr, Sumy, Poltava, Dnipropetrovsk, Zaporizhzhia, Kharkiv, Mykolaiv, Odesa, Kirovohrad, and Vinnytsia oblasts. (Source: @eRadarrua/132497)
Launch sites included Orel (5 groups) and Millerovo (2 groups) of jet-powered UAVs, per radar tracking. (Source: @eRadarrua/132499)
Kyiv air raid alert at 01:22, all-clear at 02:08; Geran-5 UAVs over Vyshhorod at 4,000m altitude and 555 km/h. (Source: @eRadarrua/132539, @eRadarrua/132573, @mon1tor_ua/78723)
Approximately 10 UAVs from the Black Sea passed Lake Sasyk toward southern Odesa region. (Source: @eRadarrua/132527)
Explosions reported at Baltiysk (Kaliningrad) Baltic Fleet base and a Russian cargo ship sinking near Gelendzhik. (Source: @UkraineNow/85449, @UkraineNow/85445)
Ukraine and UK signed agreement for joint production of middle-strike and deep-strike long-range drones in Britain, funded by UK. (Source: @UkraineNow/85454)
DeepState map shows Russian forces advanced near Novomarkove and Mykolaivka in Donetsk region. (Source: @DeepStateUA/24018)

sections.threat_assessment: The scale and depth of the November 21-22 drone attack — 186 UAVs launched simultaneously from seven axes, including 72 jet-powered Shaheds — demonstrates Russia's growing capacity to saturate Ukrainian air defenses across multiple fronts. Jet-powered UAVs achieved unprecedented penetration, overflying Kyiv at high altitude and speed, maneuvering along the Dnipro, and reaching western oblasts like Vinnytsia. The use of Orel and Millerovo as primary launch hubs for jet variants suggests a shift toward faster, harder-to-intercept platforms. Ukrainian interception of 161 targets (86%) remains high, but the 18 confirmed hits and ongoing attack at 08:00 indicate leakage under saturation. Simultaneous strikes on Russian territory (Baltiysk, Gelendzhik) signal Ukrainian long-range strike capability expanding.
sections.regional_response: NATO Secretary General Rutte affirmed Article 5 commitment to defend every inch of Poland following Russian missile airspace violations, reinforcing alliance deterrence posture. The UK-Ukraine agreement to co-produce middle-strike and deep-strike drones in Britain, with UK funding, marks a significant escalation in Western military-industrial integration and will likely accelerate Ukrainian deep-strike capacity. These developments, combined with Ukrainian strikes inside Russia (Kaliningrad, Krasnodar), raise the threshold for Russian escalation while testing NATO's red lines.
sections.intelligence_notes: Russian UAV tactics now emphasize jet-powered platforms (Shahed-238/Geran-5) capable of 555 km/h at 4,000m, complicating mobile fire group and MANPADS engagement. Launch patterns show concentration at Orel (5 groups) and Millerovo (2 groups), suggesting dedicated jet-UAV regiments. Ukrainian radar tracking (eRadar) provides real-time oblast-level granularity, enabling predictive interception. The daily 09:00 nationwide minute of silence reflects societal militarization. Notable: Russian cargo ship loss near Gelendzhik and Baltiysk explosions may indicate Ukrainian naval drone or missile operations, though attribution remains unconfirmed in source data.
